sentences.text: Apron cleanliness and stand readiness checks are treated as operational prerequisites before any surface movement release is accepted into the departure sequence.
The Ramp Control Lead defines the sweep areas by stand, taxilane, service road interface, and equipment staging zone so that each check has a clear spatial boundary.
Ground Handling Dispatcher assigns qualified personnel to perform apron sweeps during planned turnaround milestones and after any event that may introduce foreign object debris.
Foreign object debris checks cover paved stand surfaces, jet bridge wheel paths, towbar storage locations, belt loader positions, fueling lanes, and adjacent drainage grates.
East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor provide supporting surveillance cues, but visual confirmation remains required where sensor coverage is obstructed by parked aircraft or ground equipment.
The Ramp Movement Board displays stand readiness status using time-stamped states that distinguish unchecked, under inspection, cleaned, blocked, and ready conditions.
Ramp Control Lead sends the Apron Sweep Completion Note after the responsible sweep team confirms that the assigned apron area is clean, safe, and free of observed foreign object debris.
Airport CDM Portal uses the shuttle count to confirm that remote-stand passenger transfer demand is consistent with stand readiness timing.
The Airport CDM Portal records each stand readiness confirmation with the stand identifier, responsible organization, inspection time, readiness constraint, and confirming user identity.
Identity Access Service restricts readiness confirmation privileges to approved ramp, handling, and airport operations roles to prevent unverified operational releases.
Time Synchronization Service provides the common time reference for sweep records, readiness confirmations, and safety-related release decisions.
When a sweep identifies debris, leaking fluid, damaged pavement, unsecured equipment, wildlife activity, or lighting damage, the stand remains unavailable until the hazard is removed or mitigated.
Ground Handling Dispatcher updates the Handling Resource Planner when personnel, equipment, or cleaning vehicles are reassigned to restore a contaminated stand.
The Ramp Control Lead reviews unresolved hazards against active turnaround demand before allowing pushback planning to continue for the affected stand.
Tower Supervisor does not use a stand readiness indication as clearance for aircraft movement, but the indication supports coordinated surface planning and prevents premature sequencing.
Departure Metering Service suppresses release recommendations for flights whose assigned stand is not marked ready or whose access route is blocked by an unresolved apron condition.
Gate Conflict Detector checks readiness status against aircraft allocation, towing activity, and adjacent stand occupancy to identify conflicts before ground movement begins.
Airline Operations Coordinator may propose a revised Target Off Block Time when apron cleaning or stand restoration is expected to delay the planned turnaround.
Slot Allocation Engine retains the Calculated Takeoff Time until the operational delay exceeds the tolerance defined in the Business Rules Registry.
Airport Duty Manager can declare a localized Capacity Reduction State when repeated apron contamination or stand closures materially reduce usable gate capacity.
During Adverse Weather Mode, sweep intervals may be shortened because wind, precipitation, or deicing residue can increase the probability of foreign object debris and surface contamination.
Safety-related releases are timed so that the latest sweep confirmation remains valid through passenger boarding completion, equipment removal, door closure, and pushback coordination.
If the readiness validity window expires before movement begins, the stand returns to an inspection-required state and a new check is performed before release.
Audit Event Ledger stores readiness changes, user acknowledgements, hazard closures, and release decisions to support post-operation review and accountability.

Performance Analytics Warehouse uses aggregated readiness and contamination timing data to identify recurring debris locations, inefficient sweep patterns, and opportunities for preventive maintenance.
